subject: Archaeology
title: Thermoluminescence: Dating Pottery
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Thermoluminescence: Dating Pottery.

hook.text: When pottery is fired in a kiln, its internal radiation clock resets to zero. The clock has been ticking ever since.

buildup.text: Minerals in clay trap energy from background radiation. Heating the sample releases that energy as a faint glow.

discovery.text: The brighter the glow, the older the pottery. This technique — thermoluminescence — dates ceramics up to 100,000 years.

twist.text: It also catches fakes. Forged 'ancient' pottery glows faintly because it was fired recently.

climax.text: Thermoluminescence dated burned flints at a Neanderthal cave to 170,000 years — far older than radiocarbon can measure.

punchline.text: Pottery glows when you heat it. The older it is, the brighter it shines.

quiz.question: How does thermoluminescence detect forgeries?
options: Modern clay contains chemicals not found in ancient deposits
Recently fired pottery glows faintly because it has not accumulated much energy
The glaze on modern fakes reacts differently to ultraviolet light

details.summary: Thermoluminescence (TL) dating measures light released when heated ceramics are reheated in a laboratory. Minerals in clay accumulate radiation energy over time; heating releases this as light. The intensity of light emission reveals when the pottery was last fired — up to 100,000 years ago.
details.whyItMatters: TL dating fills a critical gap: it dates fired clay and burned stone, materials that radiocarbon cannot date. Since pottery is the most common artifact at most sites, this method provides dates where other techniques cannot.
takeaways: Measures light released from minerals in heated ceramics
Dates when pottery was last fired, not when clay was formed
Effective for materials up to about 100,000 years old

faq.question: How does thermoluminescence dating work in practice?
faq.answer: A pottery sample is heated in a dark laboratory. Minerals like quartz and feldspar release stored radiation energy as light. The amount of light corresponds to the radiation dose accumulated since the pottery was last fired. Combined with the local radiation rate, this gives an age estimate.

faq.question: How accurate is thermoluminescence dating compared to radiocarbon?
faq.answer: TL dating is less precise than radiocarbon, typically accurate to within 10-15% of the true age. For a 5,000-year-old pot, the uncertainty might be 500-750 years. However, it dates materials radiocarbon cannot, making it invaluable despite lower precision.
